Psychedelics and Psychedelic-Inspired Compounds for Substance Use Disorders: Are We Treating the Disease or Opening a Learning Window?
articles.abstract: Substance use disorders remain a leading cause of preventable death, and existing care is better described as disease management than as cure. Medications for opioid, alcohol, and tobacco use disorders reduce substance use, and opioid agonist treatment reduces mortality, yet retention is poor and functional recovery is rarely measured. This review asks whether psychedelics treat addiction, or temporarily create a brain state in which treatment, learning, and recovery work differently. By evaluating each pharmacologically unique compound individually, we align cellular mechanisms, animal studies and human trial data across the full spectrum of substance use disorders. Relapse prevention is not a single construct: conditioned place preference, operant reinstatement, extinction learning, and clinical abstinence index different processes, and agreement at one level does not imply agreement at another. Translational concordance is therefore indication- and compound-specific rather than a class property, with the strongest human signals for psilocybin in tobacco and alcohol use disorders, though even the alcohol signal rests on two small randomized trials with discordant results. Risk is compound-specific too: ibogaine is gated by cardiotoxicity, and ketamine carries reinforcing properties and organ toxicity of its own. Plasticity is an opportunity, not an outcome.

articles.title: Substantial Treatment-Seeking Interest, Narrow Eligibility: Diagnostic Heterogeneity and External Validity in the PRIDE Psilocybin Trial-Relevance to Precision Psychiatry.
articles.abstract: Public and patient interest in psychedelic-assisted psychotherapy is increasing, but people seeking access to psychedelic trials may be more clinically heterogeneous than the populations these trials can enrol. We conducted a cross-sectional descriptive analysis of previously unreported aggregate telephone-screening data from the coordinating site of PRIDE, an ongoing Italian multicentre phase II randomized trial comparing psilocybin with personalized neuromodulation for treatment-resistant depression (TRD). Among 67 candidates screened between November 2025 and June 2026, 54 were excluded (80.6%), eight were enrolled and treated (11.9%), and five were preliminarily eligible (7.5%). The leading reason for exclusion was absence of protocol-defined TRD or another psychiatric diagnosis (27/54, 50.0%), followed by age outside the protocol range (18.5%), current suicidal or self-harm ideation (13.0%), and substance use disorder or dependence (9.3%). The diagnostic diversity of excluded candidates highlights the gap between a narrowly defined trial population and heterogeneous treatment-seeking individuals. These screening data do not address treatment response or individualized treatment selection, but they help contextualize recruitment yield and the external validity of psychedelic trials. Trial registration: Clinical Trials Information System, EU CT No. 2024-519844-34-03.

articles.title: The nucleus accumbens: an emerging modulator in anxiety disorders.
articles.abstract: Anxiety disorders are common mental health conditions that significantly reduce quality of life and strain healthcare systems worldwide. Although traditionally known for its central role in reward processing, the nucleus accumbens (NAc) is increasingly recognized as a critical integrative node linking stress responses and motivational networks to modulate anxiety-related behaviors. This review summarizes recent findings on the NAc's role in anxiety regulation, focusing on neurotransmitter systems, including opioid receptors, oxytocin, and the endocannabinoid system, as well as glial mechanisms involving microglia and astrocytes. Additionally, we discuss the neural circuits that connect the NAc to regions such as the ventral tegmental area, the bed nucleus of the stria terminalis, and the medial prefrontal cortex, providing circuit-level insights. Emerging treatments, including pharmacological approaches such as ketamine and non-pharmacological strategies like exercise and deep brain stimulation, highlight the potential to target the NAc in anxiety disorders. Emphasizing the integration of molecular, cellular, and circuit perspectives, this review underscores the NAc's central role in anxiety regulation and calls for further research to develop more precise treatments.

articles.abstract: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is increasingly recognized as a disorder of dysfunctional neural circuits rather than solely a consequence of neurotransmitter imbalance. Although impaired synaptic plasticity has emerged as a central pathological mechanism, most studies have focused primarily on neuronal dysfunction. Astrocytes regulate synapse formation, maturation, remodeling, and elimination through perisynaptic structural support, metabolic coupling, neurotransmitter homeostasis, regulated release of neuroactive molecules, neurotrophic signaling, and neuroimmune interactions. articles.title: Participatory Drug Market Surveillance: Implications for Nursing Science and Practice.
articles.abstract: The rapidly evolving illicit drug supply presents significant challenges for clinicians, public health surveillance systems, and policymakers. Many surveillance approaches rely on delayed administrative, mortality, or healthcare data, limiting the ability to identify emerging trends in near real time. Participatory surveillance systems may provide an important complementary source of information about evolving drug markets. This study examined longitudinal and cross-national patterns in unregulated drug markets using StreetRx, a participatory surveillance platform. Data included 438,277 StreetRx submissions collected between 2013 and 2024 across the United States, Canada, Australia, the United Kingdom, Spain, France, Italy, and Germany. Drugs were classified into 13 categories using a structured coding process based on pharmacologic class and reported effects. Analyses examined temporal trends, cross-national variation, and diversity across drug categories. Findings revealed substantial changes in reported drug market activity over time. Stimulant reports increased steadily and surpassed opioid reports in several recent years, while reports of psychedelics and dissociative anesthetics increased following 2019. Opioids and benzodiazepines declined as a proportion of total reports, while diversity across drug categories increased over time. Reports of medications used for opioid use disorder were consistently identified within opioid reports. Cross-national analyses demonstrated variation in reported drug categories across participating countries. Participatory surveillance may provide timely insight into evolving drug market conditions, emerging substances, and changing patterns of demand. For addiction nursing science and practice, these systems may complement existing drug monitoring efforts by informing clinical assessment, patient education, risk reduction strategies, and future research on substance use and treatment access.

articles.title: A signaling signature distinguishes hallucinogenic from non-hallucinogenic psychedelics.
articles.abstract: Psychedelic drugs can induce intense changes in perception and thought, and some also promote long-lasting adaptations in brain circuits that are being explored for treatment of mood and anxiety disorders. How these compounds differ at the level of intracellular signaling, and how hallucinogenic drugs diverge from related non-hallucinogenic forms, is poorly understood. A central question is whether hallucinogenic serotonergic compounds are associated with intracellular signaling features that distinguish them from closely related non-hallucinogenic analogues. Here, we show that chemically diverse serotonergic psychedelics trigger a coordinated reorganization of phosphorylation patterns across many proteins in neural cells, and that this global response contains a distinct signature that separates hallucinogenic compounds from non-hallucinogenic counterparts of similar structure. We use phosphorylation of the glycolysis-regulating transcription factor FOXK2 as an example of biological follow-up from this signature and show that hallucinogenic compounds, but not their non-hallucinogenic analogues, enhance lactate accumulation. These findings indicate that hallucinogenic and non-hallucinogenic serotonergic compounds engage separable intracellular signalling architectures under defined in vitro conditions. The dataset is provided as a community resource to enable hypothesis generation and targeted mechanistic validation.

articles.title: Intravenous ketamine for major depressive episodes in routine practice: a review of non-randomized evidence on effectiveness and safety.
articles.abstract: Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) have established the acute antidepressant efficacy of intravenous racemic ketamine. However, the evidence remains limited by short-term trial durations, few long-term controlled trials of repeated administration, and the absence of a systematic program for monitoring tolerability and safety. PubMed, Embase and PsycINFO were searched from inception to 30 September 2026 for non-randomized studies of intravenous racemic ketamine in adults with a major depressive episode (MDE). Fifty-six studies were included. After induction, response ranged from 26% to 71% and remission from 14% to 53%, broadly overlapping estimates from RCTs. Durability varied, with benefits waning within weeks in many patients and relapse occurring during maintenance. Attrition was high. Blood pressure elevations were transient, with mean increases varying nearly fivefold across services. Serious adverse events were unreported in 24 studies, and urinary and hepatic outcomes were rarely reported. Intravenous ketamine is often used as maintenance therapy, yet the durability of its benefits remains uncertain, and the risks of cumulative exposure remain unquantified. Systematic collection of safety and tolerability data is needed to assess long-term safety. Head-to-head comparisons with esketamine, psychedelics, and/or accelerated transcranial magnetic stimulation are needed, alongside maintenance trials and studies addressing comorbidities and/or integrating psychotherapy modalities.

However, NDEs have been present within religious, literary, and biographical texts for centuries. The phenomenology of NDEs encompasses an inward journey wherein review of one's life, seeing the dead, and an encounter with a spiritually powerful "being of light" may be reported. The subjective transformations that take place in survivors, as well as the insights generated from NDEs, can be linked with dimensions of the depressive position and Bion's concept of

articles.title: Ketamine promotes strategic and efficient approach-avoidance conflict resolution.
articles.abstract: Adaptive behavior requires flexibly balancing approach and avoidance in risky or threatening environments, a flexibility disrupted in depression and other disorders marked by excessive avoidance. Benzodiazepines such as lorazepam broadly dampen neural excitability and synaptic plasticity, whereas ketamine may enhance both. We therefore asked whether ketamine promotes more strategic and efficient motivational behavior. In this completed randomized crossover study, 34 healthy participants with no lifetime neurological or psychiatric disorders and no regular medication use were assessed at the University Medical Center Freiburg (DRKS00025471). Participants completed three visits separated by seven days: a control visit without medication, followed by intranasal ketamine (50 mg) and oral lorazepam (1 mg) in randomized, counterbalanced order. Threat probability and loss magnitude were varied independently in a dynamic approach-avoidance conflict task conducted after ketamine's acute dissociative phase. Reported behavioral outcomes were net token gain, approach behavior, and approach and withdrawal latencies. Behavioral assessors were blinded to condition; participants and physicians were not. Mixed-effects models were used. All 34 randomized participants completed each condition and were analyzed. Ketamine yielded 57% higher token gains than control (β = 0.09, 95% confidence interval 0.05 to 0.13; p < 0.001) and 33% higher gains than lorazepam (β = 0.05, 0.01 to 0.09; p = 0.009). Behavior following ketamine was more strongly guided by outcome value than threat probability and showed faster approach and withdrawal responses. Lorazepam produced a less selective increase in approach behavior. No unexpected adverse events occurred. In healthy participants, ketamine was associated with more efficient and value-sensitive approach-avoidance behavior than control and lorazepam. Many everyday decisions involve weighing a possible gain against a possible harm. In depression, this balance shifts toward avoidance, and people withdraw from rewarding opportunities. Ketamine is a fast-acting antidepressant, but how it restores motivation is unclear. We asked 34 healthy volunteers to play a computer game in which they collected coins while avoiding a virtual attacker, once without medication, once after ketamine and once after lorazepam, a widely used calming medicine. After ketamine, volunteers earned far more coins. They acted more quickly and judged each situation better, taking chances when little could be lost and holding back when much could. Lorazepam did not produce this selective pattern. Ketamine may therefore work in depression by restoring flexible, goal-directed engagement with the environment.

articles.title: Corrigendum to "Rapid antidepressant effects of ketamine combined with selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors: Mechanisms and outlook" [J. Psychiatr. Res. 204, 380-385].
Deep learning of brain-behavior dimensions identifies transdiagnostic biotypes in youth with ADHD and anxiety disorders.
articles.abstract: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder and anxiety disorders are highly prevalent in youth and frequently co-occur, yet substantial within- and cross-disorder heterogeneity limits neurobiological specificity and complicates treatment selection. Here we conducted an observational cohort analysis and developed a deep learning framework that integrates clinically salient functional connectivity with cognitive and behavioral measures to identify interpretable transdiagnostic dimensions and biologically grounded biotypes. In 3,508 children aged 9-11 years from the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development study, the model revealed two reproducible brain-behavior dimensions reflecting cognitive control and emotion-attention regulation. These dimensions yielded three biotypes (externalizing-disinhibited, internalizing-distressed and mixed dysregulation) with distinct symptom profiles, network organization and brain development. They generalized to 224 age-matched Healthy Brain Network participants and were detectable before symptom onset, indicating preclinical expression. These findings support brain-behavior dimensions for parsing transdiagnostic heterogeneity and motivating early risk stratification and mechanism-informed intervention in youth mental health.

articles.title: How Does Psilocybin Affect Daily Life Experience and Behavior? Protocol For a Multimethod Ambulatory Assessment Study Within a Clinical Trial of Psilocybin for Depression.
articles.abstract: Although psilocybin has shown promise for treating depression, responses vary considerably, with some individuals experiencing limiting improvement and even adverse effects. Research has largely relied on assessments conducted at discrete time points, providing limited insight into how post-psilocybin change unfolds in everyday life. The Dial-In study aims to characterize daily-life processes associated with differential responses to psilocybin, including factors associated with improvement or worsening following challenging dosing experiences. Dial-In is a prospective, observational, multi-method longitudinal study embedded within a clinical trial administering 25 mg of psilocybin to up to 141 adults with major depressive disorder. Ambulatory assessments combine ecological momentary assessment (EMA) and voice diaries for 14 days pre- and post- dosing, and passive audio sampling via the Electronically Activated Recorder (EAR) for three four-day periods to characterize everyday affect, behavior, reflections, and social interactions. Outcomes include depressive symptoms, psychological well-being, and psychedelic-related adverse effects assessed through eight weeks post-dose. Analyses will examine whether affective sudden gains and losses, social support, interpersonal conflict, conversational focus, reflection and rigidity predict differential outcomes. Additional analyses will test whether these factors moderate associations between challenging dosing experiences and clinical outcomes. The project was approved by WCG Institutional Review Board, with Emory University relying on WCG as the reviewing board. All participants provide written informed consent. Findings will be disseminated through peer-reviewed publications and scientific presentations. ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT06512194 (parent trial), OSF (https://osf.io/nx5ky/overview).

articles.title: A state-dependent glymphatic dimension in major depressive disorder: implications for treatment resistance.
articles.abstract: The glymphatic system refers to cerebrospinal fluid-interstitial fluid exchange and proposed drainage pathways shaped by sleep, arousal, vascular dynamics, and astrocytic organization. This physiology offers a way to connect disturbances that often coexist in major depressive disorder (MDD): disrupted sleep, fatigue, cognitive slowing, and stress-related abnormalities. We propose that difficulty establishing or maintaining a coordinated sleep-astrocyte-vascular state may contribute to illness persistence in some patients. Treatment-resistant depression (TRD) provides a setting in which this possibility can be examined across the course of treatment. Preclinical studies link stress and depressive-like behavior to astrocytic injury, aquaporin-4 dysregulation, and altered fluid transport. Human imaging findings vary across depressive phenotypes. In a dedicated TRD study, a higher diffusion tensor imaging along the perivascular space (DTI-ALPS) ratio was partly driven by reduced denominator diffusivity, illustrating the importance of interpreting this indirect index at component level. Whole-brain spatiotemporal models provide a complementary account of the neural activity accompanying these physiological states. Ketamine/esketamine, transcranial magnetic stimulation, and chronobiological interventions offer different ways to investigate treatment-related change; serotonergic psychedelics provide an exploratory extension. Longitudinal studies can establish how changes in sleep, fluid-sensitive imaging, and neural dynamics relate temporally to clinical recovery. This Perspective therefore develops a potentially modifiable physiological dimension of persistent depressive illness and defines how it can be tested.

articles.title: Animal models in psychedelic research - Tripping over translation.
articles.abstract: Psychedelic substances show promise for treating psychiatric disorders including depression, anxiety, and PTSD, but the neurobiological mechanisms underlying their therapeutic effects remain poorly understood. Preclinical findings have so far been inconsistent, limiting mechanistic insights. We argue this translational gap is exacerbated by systematic disconnects between conditions thought to shape therapeutic outcomes in humans and those employed in animal research. In this review, we analyse 266 rodent psychedelic studies published between 2014 and 2026 in order to generate a systematic audit of experimental conditions and behavioural assays currently applied in the field. Specifically, we first assessed adherence to welfare practices paralleling "set and setting" factors critical to human therapy. We found that most studies contained stress-inducing factors: only a minority reported active-phase testing (14%), environmental enrichment (7%), or refined handling protocols (21%), while drug administration almost universally relied on stress-inducing, restraint-requiring methods. Second, we evaluated the capacity of behavioural assays to capture experiential dynamics, revealing that most studies rely on brief, constrained testing with isolated behavioural markers that fail to capture the multidimensional, temporally evolving nature of psychedelic states. Beyond these methodological gaps, we identify a third critical factor largely absent from preclinical research: individual differences and social context. Most animal studies use group-level, cross-sectional designs that cannot characterize heterogeneous treatment responses or social mechanisms implicated in therapeutic change. We propose that improving translation requires a fundamental reorientation: from brief testing of stressed, isolated animals toward longitudinal tracking of individuals in enriched social environments using comprehensive behavioural characterization. We end by offering practical advice on how to implement some of these considerations in animal psychedelic research.

Targeting CGRP signaling reverses maladaptive neurogenic immunosuppression in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma models.
articles.abstract: Neurogenic inflammation is one component that sculpts the immune milieu of solid tumors. However, it remains unclear how the sensory-neuroimmune axis shapes the immune microenvironment in cold tumors to bolster treatment resistance. Using orthotopic head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) models, we demonstrate tumor growth-induced sensory hyperexcitability, and that surgical sensory signaling interruption reduced tumor growth. Genetic knockout of a key neuropeptide released by sensory neurons, calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP), encoded by Calca, produced eradication when paired with radioimmunotherapy. Such treatment reduced Treg infiltration and immunosuppressive function in Calca knockout mice. We also observed that high-dose psilocybin functions as a CGRP inhibitor and transiently reduces tumor growth by increasing antitumor immunity. Additionally, psilocybin increased circulating serotonin, which was partially reversed with platelet activation inhibitor, clopidogrel. We observed differential effects on CD8 and Treg functionality by psilocin in vitro. Correlational analyses in plasma from human subjects following a single-dose psilocybin corroborated these findings. Together, this work underscores the complex interaction of neurogenic inflammation and the tumor immune microenvironment, highlighting a potential therapeutic avenue for HNSCC and other solid tumors.

articles.title: A let-7a-5p-engineered extracellular vesicle-laden bioactive scaffold promotes immunomodulation and regeneration of segmental tracheal defects.
articles.abstract: Segmental tracheal defects resulting from trauma, tumor resection, or congenital malformations pose significant challenges for reconstruction. Persistent post-injury inflammation, inadequate neovascularization, and delayed epithelial restoration contribute to the formation of granulation tissue and subsequent graft failure. In this study, we developed a bioactive tracheal scaffold for sustained local delivery of let-7a-5p-engineered extracellular vesicles (let-7a-5p-EVs) to modulate the regenerative microenvironment during tracheal repair. The scaffold was constructed by integrating a mechanically optimized polycaprolactone (PCL) framework with a 20% Pluronic F127 hydrogel, which served as a local reservoir for EV retention and sustained release. Let-7a-5p-EVs were generated from lentivirally engineered human gingiva-derived mesenchymal stem cells and showed typical EV morphology, representative EV marker expression, and efficient uptake by airway epithelial cells. In vitro, let-7a-5p-EVs enhanced airway epithelial cell migration and shifted lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced macrophages from a pro-inflammatory M1-like phenotype toward a reparative M2-like phenotype, accompanied by reduced inflammatory cytokine expression. In a rabbit segmental tracheal defect model, the let-7a-5p-EV-laden scaffold enhanced neovascularization, mitigated local inflammatory responses, promoted mucociliary epithelial reconstruction, and maintained airway patency. The let-7a-5p-EV scaffold improved biomechanical recovery, and increased survival rates. Transcriptomic profiling and molecular validation indicated that these effects were associated with the attenuation of nuclear factor kappa B (NF-κB)-associated inflammatory activation, as evidenced by reduced p65 phosphorylation and nuclear localization. These findings demonstrate that sustained local delivery of engineered EVs from a mechanically competent bioactive scaffold provides an effective immunomodulatory strategy for the regenerative repair of segmental tracheal defects and offers translational potential for functional airway reconstruction.

articles.title: Update on Sedation for Upper Gastrointestinal Endoscopy in Japan: Current Evidence on Remimazolam.
articles.abstract: Sedation is an essential component of upper gastrointestinal endoscopy because it reduces patient discomfort and anxiety while improving patient acceptance and procedural quality. In Japan, benzodiazepines such as midazolam and opioid analgesics have long been widely used in routine clinical practice; however, many of these agents historically lacked formal insurance approval for sedation during gastrointestinal endoscopy. Propofol is also a useful sedative because of its rapid onset and recovery, but its use in Japan has been limited because of concerns regarding respiratory and cardiovascular depression and the need for management by anesthesia-trained personnel. Against this background, the approval of remimazolam for sedation during gastrointestinal endoscopy in June 2025 represented a major turning point in Japanese endoscopic sedation practice. Remimazolam is an ultra-short-acting benzodiazepine rapidly metabolized by carboxylesterases and reversible with flumazenil. Japanese phase III trials demonstrated high sedation success rates and rapid recovery during upper gastrointestinal endoscopy, including in elderly patients. Compared with midazolam, remimazolam shortened awakening and ambulation times, whereas compared with propofol, it may cause fewer respiratory and cardiovascular adverse events. This review summarizes the current status of upper gastrointestinal endoscopic sedation in Japan, focusing on the clinical evidence and positioning of the newly approved ultra-short-acting benzodiazepine, remimazolam.

articles.title: 3D printed Bouncy Bioglass enhances articular cartilage regeneration.
articles.abstract: Articular cartilage is an avascular tissue with limited intrinsic repair capacity, and untreated defects will deteriorate progressively over time. Lining the ends of bones, it plays a critical role in joint lubrication and shock absorption. Current surgical interventions, such as microfracture, typically result in the formation of mechanically inferior fibrocartilage. There remains a significant unmet clinical need for biomaterials that can support the regeneration of functional articular cartilage. We present a non-cytotoxic sol-gel hybrid scaffold, of composition silica/poly(tetrahydrofuran)/polycaprolactone (SiO<sub>2</sub>/PTHF/PCL-diCOOH), termed 'Bouncy Bioglass' to address that need. Our ovine model revealed that Bouncy Bioglass scaffolds with 250 μm channels stimulated hyaline cartilage regeneration. They outperformed scaffolds with 500 μm channel and microfracture alone, by improved integration and filling of the defect site with articular-like cartilage tissue. This tissue showed a significant increase in collagen type II and other primary components of healthy articular cartilage, compared to the tissue formed from the other two conditions. Our hybrid biomaterial, Bouncy Bioglass, enhances the regeneration of articular cartilage and may offer an 'off-the-shelf' synthetic implant option to treat localised articular defects and prevent their continued degeneration.

articles.title: Pain Management in the Trauma Patient.
articles.abstract: Effective pain management in adult trauma patients is essential to improve recovery, reduce complications, and prevent long-term consequences such as chronic pain, depression, and PTSD. Multimodal analgesia combines medications and nonpharmacologic strategies to achieve better pain control while minimizing opioid use and associated risks. Key agents include acetaminophen, nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory agents, ketamine, topical and systemic lidocaine, gabapentinoids, muscle relaxants, and carefully selected opioids when necessary. Pain management should be individualized based on patient factors, including age, comorbidities, traumatic brain injury, and substance use disorders. Early assessment, regular reassessment, and coordinated multidisciplinary care optimize outcomes across trauma settings.

articles.title: MDMA-assisted therapy for social anxiety disorder: A randomized, open-label, wait-list controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
Background

±3, 4-methylenedioxymethamphetamine (MDMA) has positive effects on socio-emotional processing and MDMA-Assisted Therapy (MDMA-AT) showed promise for treating Social Anxiety Disorder (SAD) in a previous placebo-controlled trial.

Aims

Develop a preliminary estimate of clinical response and safety for MDMA-AT versus waitlist in adults with SAD. Secondary aims included refinement of a standardized psychotherapy manual and assessment of candidate therapeutic processes.

Method

This randomized, open-label, wait-list controlled clinical trial recruited and enrolled 20 participants diagnosed with SAD from April 2022 to March 2024. They were randomly assigned to either immediate treatment with MDMA-AT or a 16-week waitlist condition followed by MDMA-AT equivalent to the immediate treatment arm. MDMA-AT consisted of three 90-min preparation sessions, two MDMA sessions, and six 90-min integration sessions. The preregistered primary outcome was the Liebowitz Social Anxiety Scale; secondary outcomes were functioning, shame, acceptance, belongingness, self-concealment, and self-compassion.

Results

Across 20 participants (45% women, 40% men, 15% transgender; 85% White; mean age 38) we observed a mean difference on the Liebowitz Social Anxiety Scale at 16-week primary outcome of -43.3 (SD = 14.7; 95% CI, -29.5 to -57.1; p < .0001; Hedges' g = 2.8) indicating greater improvement in the MDMA-AT condition. No serious adverse events occurred; adverse events were mild to moderate and transient.

Conclusions

MDMA-AT resulted in a significant reduction in social anxiety symptoms and improvement in functioning compared to waitlist. There were no serious adverse events. Findings provide preliminary data for clinical response, safety, and feasibility of MDMA-AT for SAD, supporting the need for further investigation. articles.title: A psychedelic-rich alkaloid fraction obtained from Mimosa tenuiflora (Willd.) Poir attenuates somatic and affective symptoms of naloxone-precipitated morphine withdrawal in C57BL/6 mice.
articles.abstract:
Ethnopharmacological relevance

Mimosa tenuiflora (Willd.) Poir. root bark is traditionally used in northeastern Brazil to prepare "Jurema wine", a beverage employed to relieve emotional distress and restore psychological well-being. However, validating its traditional preparations in central substance withdrawal states remains underexplored.

Aim of the study

To evaluate the ethnopharmacological potential of M. tenuiflora, we investigated the effects of an alkaloid fraction (AF II) from its root bark on somatic and affective morphine withdrawal symptoms in mice, without compromising analgesia.

Materials and methods

Male C57BL/6 mice were used for the tests. Possible interference with morphine-induced analgesia was assessed using the acetic acid-induced writhing test. The animals were made morphine-dependent using a dose-escalation regimen, and withdrawal syndrome was precipitated with naloxone. AF II (3, 6, or 9 mg/kg, s.c.) was administered before withdrawal induction.

Results

AF II did not interfere with morphine analgesia. AF II significantly reduced key somatic signs of morphine withdrawal, decreasing jumping and paw tremor without affecting Walk in reverse. During withdrawal, AF II increased exploratory behavior in the open field and modulated anxiety-related parameters.

Conclusions

The AF II from Mimosa tenuiflora, rich in serotonergic compounds, selectively attenuates somatic and affective components of opioid withdrawal in mice without compromising opioid analgesia, supporting its potential as a preliminary candidate for acute opioid withdrawal modulation. These findings provide scientific support for the traditional knowledge surrounding the central psychoactive and restorative properties of M. tenuiflora preparations.

articles.title: Tissue engineering polymeric formulations enable lymphangiogenesis for myocardial repair.
articles.abstract:
Purpose

Emerging evidence emphasizes the pivotal contribution of cardiac lymphatic activation following ischemic heart injury, with induced lymphangiogenesis driving edema resolution and inflammatory cell clearance. The aim of this study was to identify a bioactive small molecule with pro-lymphangiogenic activity and to develop a tissue engineering polymeric formulation for sustained local delivery in myocardial repair.

Methods

Through a high-throughput screen, we identified the bioactive molecule β-(3,4-dihydroxyphenyl) lactic acid (3,4-DHPLA) as a potent stimulator of lymphatic endothelial cells (LECs). To leverage this finding, we engineered a tissue engineering polymeric formulation (TEPF) to promote lymphangiogenesis during myocardial repair. The TEPF was fabricated via an integrated strategy combining 3D printing and near-field electrospinning to incorporate 3,4-DHPLA into a biodegradable polyurethane scaffold. The resulting structure mimics the microstructure of the cardiac extracellular matrix while supporting the microenvironment-responsive release of 3,4-DHPLA.

Results

We evaluated the therapeutic efficacy of TEPF in rat and porcine ischemia/reperfusion injury models, which markedly improved cardiac function and significantly attenuated adverse ventricular remodeling. Single-cell RNA sequencing and in vitro data further revealed the dual mechanisms of TEPF, not only promoting lymphangiogenesis but also orchestrating a pro-regenerative niche via expansion of Tregs, M2 macrophages, and pro-regenerative fibroblasts (COL12A1+, COL11A1+, NRG1+).

Conclusions

Thus, the tissue engineering polymeric formulations may enable sustained drug release during myocardial tissue repair, thereby alleviating the pain of injection administration for patients with cardiovascular diseases and potentially facilitating patient-friendly use of other functional molecules-based therapeutic tissue engineering formulations through durable delivery.

articles.title: Glis1 regulates metabolic programming by promoting H3K18 lactylation to alleviate neuronal senescence following spinal cord injury.
articles.abstract: Neuronal senescence is a significant factor impeding spinal cord injury (SCI) repair. Research indicates that Glis1, a Kruppel-like zinc finger transcription factor, is pivotal in reprogramming senescent cells and enhancing genomic stability via lactylation. Histone lactylation, an epigenetic modification using lactate as a substrate, becomes prominent post-SCI due to increased neuronal lactate levels. However, the mechanisms linking neuronal senescence and histone lactylation following SCI remain poorly understood. This study elucidates the roles of Glis1, H3K18 lactylation, and neuronal senescence through comprehensive in vivo and in vitro investigations. The findings reveal a post-SCI rise in neuronal lactate levels, accompanied by cellular senescence. Furthermore, upregulation of Glis1 attenuates senescence and promotes histone lactylation. The downstream target secretogranin II (SCG2), identified via ChIP-seq and RNA-seq, was found to exert negative feedback on glycolytic metabolism and lactylation, thereby suppressing neuronal senescence. These results unveil a novel regulatory mechanism of Glis1 in neuronal senescence following SCI through the p300/H3K18la/SCG2 axis, offering a new therapeutic target for spinal cord repair.

articles.title: Unveiling Ayahuasca: Comprehensive study of botanical and chemical diversity.
articles.abstract:
Ayahuasca is an entheogenic beverage traditionally used by Indigenous peoples and local communities throughout Amazonia. Its preparation typically involves the vine Banisteriopsis caapi and the leaves of Psychotria viridis, widely recognized as its principal ingredients. Other plant species and ethnotaxa have also been historically reported in association with ayahuasca preparation, but their identities and supporting evidence remain unclear.

Aim of the study

This study compiles plant species and ethnotaxa historically reported in association with ayahuasca preparation and evaluates the ethnobotanical, taxonomic, and phytochemical evidence supporting these records.

Materials and methods

A narrative review of ethnobotanical and phytochemical literature was integrated with herbarium voucher data. Species were assessed according to the strength of available evidence, including peer-reviewed records, herbarium voucher records associated with vernacular names, and current taxonomic concepts. This framework distinguished taxa with robust support from those with limited documentation.

Results

Twenty-four vine species (Malpighiaceae) and thirteen species reported as leaf ingredients (Malpighiaceae and Rubiaceae) were identified, together with 119 B. caapi and two P. viridis ethnotaxa. Five vine and four leaf species were supported by both literature and voucher records and classified as historically confirmed ingredients. Ten vine and three leaf species were supported only by voucher records and classified as putative ayahuasca-associated taxa, whereas nine vine and six leaf species lacked sufficient evidence and were excluded. In addition, eighty species were identified as occasional additives to the ayahuasca beverage. Phytochemical data remain heavily concentrated on B. caapi and P. viridis.

Conclusions

Ayahuasca is associated with greater botanical diversity than is currently recognized, although supporting evidence varies among taxa. An evidence-based framework is essential for distinguishing historically supported ingredients from putative taxa and for guiding future research.

articles.title: A bioactivity-enhanced thermosensitive amnion-derived hydrogel with sustained IGF-1 release: A multitargeted and efficient strategy for corneal injury repair.
articles.abstract: Corneal alkali burn (CAB) remains difficult to treat because rapid tear clearance limits topical drug exposure, while the injured cornea develops a complex microenvironment involving inflammation, neovascularization, fibrosis, epithelial barrier loss, and impaired nerve repair. Here, we developed a human amniotic membrane-derived thermosensitive hydrogel (hAMgel) and loaded it with insulin-like growth factor-1 (IGF-1) to create a bioactive sustained-release system (IGF1@hAMgel) for CAB repair. The hAMgel transformed from a flowable precursor into a semi-transparent film on the ocular surface within 1-2 min and IGF1@hAMgel released approximately 90% of loaded IGF-1 over 24 h, with corneal IGF-1 concentration peaking at 2 h post-dose (378.5 pg/mg protein) and remaining detectable over 24 h, supporting sustained topical exposure. In a rat CAB model, IGF1@hAMgel accelerated epithelial healing, reducing the fluorescein-stained area from 31.34 ± 2.83% in controls to 16.78 ± 2.87% at day 1. By day 14, IGF1@hAMgel reduced corneal opacity (0.67 ± 0.52 vs. 4.00 ± 0.00), resolved edema with central corneal thickness approaching baseline (187.7 ± 16.31 μm vs. 178.3 ± 5.89 μm), suppressed neovascularization (CD31-positive area 4.46 ± 1.69% vs. 24.33 ± 2.07%), and promoted corneal nerve regeneration. Proteomic analysis showed that hAMgel retained abundant extracellular matrix(ECM) components, including collagens, Lumican, and fibronectin, together with repair-related and immunomodulatory proteins. These findings identify IGF1@hAMgel as a sutureless, eye-drop-like bioactive ECM platform that integrates growth-factor delivery with amnion-derived reparative cues for multitargeted ocular surface repair.

Subacute and long-term changes in cognitive functioning after administration of classic psychedelics, MDMA and ketamine: A systematic review of clinical and preclinical evidence
articles.abstract: Psychedelic agents induce a window of heightened neuroplasticity that extends beyond acute intoxication, during which neural circuits are more amenable to change. This period may facilitate changes in cognition relevant to the treatment of psychiatric disorders. This systematic review synthesised clinical and preclinical evidence of subacute and long-term (≥1 day) effects of classic and non-classic psychedelics on cognition. MEDLINE, EMBASE, APA PsycInfo and Web of Science were searched to identify human and animal studies investigating psychedelics and cognition (executive function, attention, decision-making). Sixty-seven (47 clinical, 20 preclinical) articles met inclusion criteria. Psilocybin demonstrated the most consistent evidence of subacute and longer-term cognitive improvement, particularly in cognitive flexibility and attention. Ketamine showed enhancement across cognitive domains, although findings were heterogeneous. LSD and DMT showed no consistent subacute changes, while MDMA was associated with transient cognitive impairments that resolved within days. Risk of bias assessments revealed selective outcome reporting, poor reporting of missing data and inadequate methodological detail, limiting the confidence of findings. Current evidence provides preliminary support for subacute changes in cognition following administration of select psychedelic agents. Cognitive improvements were more frequently seen in psychiatric populations than healthy subjects, which may re

articles.title: Psychedelics and autism spectrum disorder: Mechanistic insights, translational evidence and ethical challenges
articles.abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a heterogeneous neurodevelopmental condition characterized by persistent deficits in social communication and interaction, restricted and repetitive patterns of behavior, and sensory processing alterations, frequently accompanied by anxiety, emotional dysregulation, and other psychiatric comorbidities. Despite advances in behavioral and pharmacological interventions, effective treatments for core ASD symptoms remain limited. Psychedelic compounds have recently emerged as potential therapeutic agents in psychiatry because of their ability to modulate serotonergic and glutamatergic signaling, enhance neuroplasticity, reorganize large-scale brain networks, and influence neurobiological pathways implicated in ASD. In this narrative review, we examine the mechanistic rationale supporting psychedelic-based approaches in ASD, including 5-HT2A receptor activation, oxytocin-serotonin interactions, excitation-inhibition dynamics, functional connectivity, and glutamatergic modulation associated with ketamine and related compounds. We also summarize current clinical and preclinical evidence involving substances such as psilocybin, lysergic acid diethylamide, 3,4-methylenedioxymethamphetamine, and ketamine. Particular attention is given to the distinction between core ASD symptoms and associated symptom domains. Current evidence does not support the direct treatment of core social communication deficits or restricted and repetitive behaviors; however, psy

articles.title: Prevalence and Reasons for Microdosing Cannabis, Psilocybin, LSD, and MDMA Among U.S. Adults
articles.abstract: Microdosing involves consuming low doses of psychoactive substances, typically 1/5th to 1/20th of a recreational dose. Despite increasing public attention to cannabis and psychedelics amid evolving drug policies, epidemiological data on microdosing remain limited.A cross-sectional, web-based survey (Characterizing the Epidemiology of Cannabidiol Use Survey) of 1,525 US adults was conducted in October-November 2023 and analyzed in 2024-2025 using Ipsos KnowledgePanel. Participants reported lifetime microdosing of cannabis, psilocybin, lysergic acid diethylamide (LSD), and 3,4-Methylenedioxymethamphetamine (MDMA). Lifetime prevalence, frequency, and reasons for microdosing were assessed, along with associations with demographics, mental health, quality of life, and cannabis and psychedelic policy environments. Survey weights were applied to generate nationally representative estimates.Cannabis was the most commonly microdosed substance (9.4%; 95% CI=8.0, 10.7; 24.1 million adults), followed by psilocybin (5.3%; 95% CI=4.3, 6.3; 13.7 million adults), LSD (4.8%; 95% CI=3.8, 5.9; 12.4 million adults), and MDMA (2.2%; 95% CI=1.5, 2.9; 5.7 million adults). Cannabis (41.2%; 95% CI=33.3, 49.5) was primarily microdosed for medical purposes (e.g., "to manage pain"), while psilocybin (66.6%; 95% CI=56.9, 75.1), LSD (59.2%; 95% CI=46.5, 70.8) and MDMA (86.0%; 95% CI=68.8, 94.5) were more commonly microdosed for recreational purposes (e.g., "to get less high"). articles.title: Microdosing psychedelics: What, why, when, and how often? Insights from an international survey of people who use psychedelics
articles.abstract: The interest in microdosing psychedelics continues to grow within academic and recreational contexts. However, microdosing practices have changed over time, and warrants examination of use patterns within a large, global sample of consumers.The Global Psychedelic Survey 2025 (GPS 2025) was an online, anonymous, cross-sectional survey conducted from May 1-23, 2025. The survey was available in 19 languages and inquired about a wide range of topics surrounding psychedelic use. This manuscript focuses on the primary outcomes for the microdosing component of the survey, examining the substances consumed, dosing regimens employed, reasons for use, as well as the typical 'set and setting' while microdosing.In this sample, 5399 participants reported microdosing during their lifetime, of whom 69.8% (n = 3768) used a microdose within the past year. Psilocybin was the most commonly microdosed substance (n = 4377; 81.1%, 95% CI: 80.0%-82.1%), followed by LSD (n = 2136; 39.6%, 95% CI: 38.3%-40.9%). This was consistent across global regions. The 'Fadiman protocol' (i.e. one day on, two days off) was the most reported dosing regimen among regular microdosers (n = 1203; 24.3%, 95% CI: 23.1%-25.6%). While microdosing, respondents reported often spending time in nature (n = 3087; 58.9%), focusing inwards (n = 2977; 56.8%), or spending leisure time (n = 2253; 43%), demonstrating preliminary evidence supporting the integration of set and setting in the context of microdosing.This study provides

articles.title: Blinding integrity in psychedelic research: Evidence from a comparative randomized controlled trial of psilocybin, MDMA, and methylphenidate in healthy volunteers
articles.abstract: Maintaining effective blinding is a major methodological challenge in psychedelic research. This study provides a comprehensive evaluation of blinding integrity in 120 healthy volunteers who received either psilocybin, MDMA, or methylphenidate (active placebo) in a double-blind, randomized controlled trial. Using a multi-level assessment incorporating forced-choice substance guesses, certainty ratings, decision factors, and subjective substance effects, the analyses characterize blinding integrity and its relation to the substance experience. Results indicate that overall blinding was insufficient, with psilocybin showing the highest rates of functional unblinding, MDMA moderate levels, and methylphenidate the lowest. As an active placebo, methylphenidate provided more effective blinding for MDMA than for psilocybin. Incorporating certainty levels of substance guesses revealed a more differentiated pattern, with lower functional unblinding rates. Decision factors and subjective substance experiences were associated with phenomenological substance effects. Prior substance experiences did not influence accuracy of forced-choice substance guesses. These findings provide empirical guidance for the design and reporting of blinding procedures in psychedelic trials and underscore the value of systematic, multi-level assessment of blinding integrity.

articles.title: Considerations for Scaling Psychedelics: Context, Reimbursement, and the Role of the Pharmacy Benefit Manager
articles.abstract: Psychedelic therapies have shown considerable promise in clinical trials, but their effects depend heavily on context—set, setting, therapeutic relationship, and integration—in ways that sit uneasily with health care systems built to finance discrete drugs and billable services. This white paper examines the institutional pathway through which psychedelic therapies may reach patients, from regulatory approval to clinical delivery, payment, and practical access. It reviews the emerging cost-effectiveness literature and identifies three challenges for coverage: valuation (what counts as benefit), duration (the Durability–Churn and Durability–Revenue dilemmas), and delivery (labor intensity and delivery design). It describes a Context–Reimbursement Paradox: the more central context is to therapeutic effect, the harder the intervention is to translate into units that existing payment systems recognize. It then analyzes where pharmacy benefit managers (PBMs) fit along a gradient of compatibility, from SSRIs to psilocybin therapy, and argues that drug pricing decisions will shape their role. It closes by considering Indigenous knowledge systems and non-medical pathways to access.

articles.title: Psilocybin and Contrasting Musical Compositions: Effects on Music-Evoked Emotional Responses in Healthy Adults
articles.abstract: <jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>                 <jats:p>Music is a central component of psychedelic settings, yet little experimental work has examined how psilocybin and musical composition influence music-evoked emotional responses in healthy volunteers. This exploratory, double-blind, placebo-controlled study assessed these effects during the plateau phase of psilocybin and the corresponding time window in placebo sessions following oral administration of psilocybin (0.26 mg/kg) or placebo. The study consisted of two parts. In Part 1 (n = 19), a pilot stage, the first half of participants rated music-induced affective valence for eight compositions representing different genres/subgenres (Rock/Punk, Metal/Industrial Metal, Metal/Industrial Metal, Classical/Baroque, Electronic/Dub, Folk/Nordic Folk, Electronic/Techno, Electronic/Trance, Electronic/Psytrance) using a visual analogue scale (VAS). Based on Part 1, the classical composition with the highest overall affective valence and the psytrance composition with the largest psilocybin–placebo contrast (i.e., the composition most responsive to psilocybin) were selected for Part 2 (n = 17), in which the second half of participants assessed emotional responses to music using the Geneva Emotional Music Scale (GEMS-9). Psilocybin increased wonder, transcendence, and joyful activation across both contrasting compositions. Relative to each other, the classical composition elicited greater peacefulness, tenderness, and nostalgia

articles.title: Acute psilocybin or ethocybin leads to a sustained increase in Pavlovian aversion memory in male mice
articles.abstract: <jats:p>There is considerable interest in the concept that psychedelic compounds might facilitate reorganization of emotional processing with therapeutic benefit; in particular, amelioration of excessive focus on past, current and potential-future aversive events, a dominant emotional-cognitive state in stress-related affective disorders. Translational animal models can advance understanding of specific aspects of this concept, namely, those relating to subconscious emotional memories and their neurobiology. In male mice, chronic social stress (CSS) leads to excessive tone/context-foot shock Pavlovian aversion learning (PAL) and memory (PAM), measured as time spent in freezing behavior, and provides a model for generalized excessive focus on aversion. Sub-chronic administration of SSRI antidepressant between PAL and PAM reverses the excessive PAM of CSS mice. Here we applied the model to investigate acute and sustained behavioral and neurobiological effects of psilocybin (PSY) and ethocybin (ETH). In control male mice, both psychedelics at 3 mg/kg per os resulted in 1–2 h of blood-brain exposure to the respective major metabolites psilocin and ethocin, and to head twitch responses. In the main experiment, mice underwent either 15-day CSS or control handling (CON), followed 2 days later by PAL, 1 day later by PSY, ETH or vehicle (VEH), and 3 days later by PAM testing and then brain collection. articles.title: EFFICACY AND SAFETY OF PSILOCYBIN IN TREATMENT-RESISTANT DEPRESSION: A REVIEW
articles.abstract: <jats:p>Major depressive disorder (MDD) is one of the leading causes of disability worldwide. A substantial proportion of patients fail to achieve remission through standard monoaminergic therapies, meeting the clinical criteria for treatment-resistant depression (TRD). TRD is associated with significant clinical morbidity and a profound economic burden on healthcare systems. This review evaluates the clinical efficacy, safety profile, and neurobiological mechanisms of psilocybin, a serotonergic psychedelic, as a targeted intervention for TRD. Current neurobiological evidence indicates that psilocybin, upon conversion to its active metabolite psilocin, acts primarily as a 5-HT2A receptor agonist. This mechanism promotes rapid structural neuroplasticity and modulates the aberrant functional connectivity characteristic of severe depression. Recent randomized clinical trials demonstrate that psilocybin, when administered in controlled settings with psychological support, produces rapid and clinically significant reductions in depressive symptoms. Comparative data indicate that its therapeutic efficacy is at least comparable to standard first-line treatments, such as SSRIs, while frequently offering a faster onset of action. Regarding safety, psilocybin is generally well-tolerated in clinical environments; adverse events are typically mild to moderate and transient. However, the strict requirement for concurrent psychological support and rigorous psychiatric screening highlights

articles.title: Development and Psychometric Validation of the ‘Psychedelic Flourishing Scale’
articles.abstract: Positive psychological changes following psychedelic experiences are widely studied, yet no validated instrument has been developed specifically to assess the breadth of enduring change that individuals attribute to those experiences. We therefore conducted a two-part programme of research to evaluate an existing measure and to develop and validate a more comprehensive scale. In Part 1, a preliminary psychometric analysis of the 11-item Mindset Questionnaire (MQ) was conducted using data from two psilocybin studies (N = 97). Its items were strongly intercorrelated (mean inter-item r = .63) and predominantly reflected a single, relatively narrow dimension of change. Part 2 followed established scale-development procedures to define the broader construct of psychedelic flourishing and develop the Psychedelic Flourishing Scale (PFS). A three-round Delphi study involving 17 experts established the construct definition and generated a 41-item pool. The PFS was then evaluated in a pre-registered cross-sectional survey of 1,296 adults who reported previous serotonergic (“classic”) psychedelic use. The sample was randomly divided for exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses, with the structure extracted in the exploratory half rather than specified in advance. In the confirmatory subsample, a model comprising five correlated facets showed good fit (RMSEA = .053, CFI = .965) and fitted better than a unidimensional model, although a four-factor model performed similarly.
